transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reed, Samir Kaur, Liam O'Connor, Priya Desai, (internal SEs join later)

Summary: quick enablement focused on messaging, competitive positioning, and demo practice. We ran two demo scenarios (hosted API vs dedicated) and practiced objection responses for latency/cost questions.

[00:00] Jordan: alright everyone, thanks for joining, uh we got about 75 minutes, agenda is messaging refresh, quick competitor notes, and then two practice demos, one focused on hosted flows and one on dedicated/private deployment.
[00:23] Samir: yeah i got a few slides, i'll kick off with where customers are tripping up on the value props, then we'll jump into the demo — please interrupt if something sounds off.
[00:38] Priya: quick ask, can we record the role-play and make a short highlight for new hires?
[00:44] Jordan: yep will do, liam can you make sure that gets into the enablement folder?
[00:49] Liam: noted, i'll upload after the call.
[01:05] Samir: ok, messaging — top thing: customers are primarily choosing based on unit cost and latency; messaging that resonates is "predictable inference economics" and "same API across hosted, dedicated, private". Use the phrase "production-first" rather than just "fast".
[01:27] Jordan: good. and remember to call out the rollout controls — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to cheaper variants — customers like the guardrails.
[01:40] Samir: yeah i'll add a slide. Another common question: why Redwood vs OpenAI or Anthropic — short answer: we give predictable SLOs, cost controls (batching/caching), and routing so you can optimize cost without building the infra.
[02:03] Samir: folks sometimes ask about Bedrock — important to note: Bedrock ties you to specific cloud provider tooling, we emphasize multi-mode deployment and easier on-prem options.
[02:18] Jordan: call out compliance wins too — SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS support, audit logs — especially for mid-market/enterprise.
[02:30] Priya: should we hand customers the compliance pack or just surface the summary?
[02:35] Jordan: surface summary in sales, send the pack on request. keep it lightweight in initial outreach.
[02:45] [demo prep noise — screen share cues]
[03:00] Samir: demo one, hosted API, goal: show latency and quality tradeoffs and the streaming experience. i'll simulate a customer request for a summarization + follow-up Q.
[03:25] Samir: (typing) "API call: model=redwood-base-1, prompt=long meeting notes, streaming=true" — watch how tokens arrive; emphasize prefix caching when we do repeated summarizations.
[03:48] Speaker 1: hmm can you explain prefix caching in the demo, sounds a bit abstract to customers.
[03:56] Samir: sure—plain language: "we cache repeated context so follow-up questions are quicker and cheaper because we don't re-send the whole prompt every time".
[04:12] Jordan: also mention continuous batching for throughput gains during spikes — makes dedicated capacity less necessary in some mid-market cases.
[04:25] Samir: good point.
[04:40] [00:04:55] Samir: small flub — the streaming UI looked choppy, maybe adjust the refresh rate.
[05:05] Jordan: note for demo script, be explicit about token cost when streaming vs non-streaming. customers like that transparency.
[05:30] [05:30] Role-play starts — Jordan as customer, Samir as SE.
[05:35] Jordan (customer): we're worried about latency spikes with high concurrency, what guarantees do you provide?
[05:42] Samir (SE): we offer Dedicated pools for predictable throughput; on hosted we have routing policies and autoscale with burst capacity plus fallbacks to compatible model variants. for SLAs, mention dedicated contracts.
[06:05] Jordan: customer probe — is fallback automatic?
[06:08] Samir: yes, automatic per-route policy, and you can opt-out if you need strict model parity.
[06:15] Jordan: nice.
[06:20] [06:20] Jordan (customer): how do you handle sensitive data — will my data be used to train models?
[06:28] Samir: short answer: we have no training-on-customer-data by default; private deployments and dedicated have stronger isolation, and we support customer-managed KMS. refer them to the security pack for details.
[06:45] Jordan: add an anecdote about a retail customer that needed PCI-adjacent compliance — that helps.
[07:00] Samir: noted.
[07:10] [07:10] Second demo prep — dedicated/private deployment scenario. Samir will show VPC flow, KMS key setup, and routing policy.
[07:25] Samir: (walkthrough) deployment page -> create private cluster -> select VPC peering -> attach KMS key. quick note: demo uses obfuscated names to avoid real keys.
[07:45] Speaker 2: tends to be the part where sales get into too many infra details — keep it at high level unless customer asks.
[07:55] Samir: agreed — show the flow, then point to the docs for step-by-step.
[08:05] [08:05] Jordan: objection handling practice — competitor angle, "we're already on Bedrock/OpenAI". Samir, play the response.
[08:12] Samir: "Great — if you already have models running, we can help on the serving side with consistent SLAs and transparent unit economics; we also support migration paths and can do a short benchmark where we run your workload and show per-token costs and latency."
[08:35] Jordan: add a line about model variants and quantization options to reduce cost.
[08:42] Samir: will include.
[09:01] [09:01] Role-play three — price objection.
[09:06] Jordan (customer): your per-token looks higher than their cheapest option.
[09:11] Samir: reference TCO and time-to-market; explain how batching/caching reduces per-request cost and how reserved Dedicated capacity can lower unit price under commit. use a quick back-of-envelope example.
[09:35] Jordan: good, but make sure we state concrete numbers in the playbook.
[09:42] Samir: noted. i'll add a slide with sample math (e.g., batching reduces token cost by ~20-40% depending on workload).
[10:00] [10:00] Break — quick logistics, pull in a couple junior SEs to observe role-play.
[12:30] [12:30] Observers join, brief intros.
[12:50] Samir: demo two redo — try to keep the handoffs tighter and reduce ums.
[13:10] [13:10] Live demo glitch — screen froze for a few seconds, Samir: "sorry — reconnecting"; Jordan: "call this out as a rare demo fluke, not a product problem".
[13:35] Jordan: pro tip: have a canned backup video or screenshot flow if live demo goes sideways. 
[13:48] Priya: we'll add that into the demo playbook.
[14:00] [14:00] Practice answering security deep-dive questions — Samir handled KMS/SSO/SOC2, but the audience asked about audit log retention and legal e-discovery.
[14:18] Samir: for audit logs we surface per-route traces and support export to SIEM; retention windows vary by plan and can be extended in enterprise contracts.
[14:35] Jordan: also note the Private on-prem package for air-gapped needs; good to have a short checklist for procurement calls.
[14:50] [14:50] Time-sliced benchmark mention — Liam: "we should have a one-page benchmark template: workload, model, seq-len, hardware, quantization, throughput".
[15:02] Liam: i'll build the template and link in the playbook.
[15:12] [15:12] Final role-play — show concise close. Jordan (customer): "what's the next step if we want to pilot?" Samir: "we propose a 4-week POC: we onboard a dataset, run benchmarks, configure routing and caching, and deliver a cost/latency report and recommended model profile."
[15:35] Jordan: that was crisp. good standard POC language.
[15:45] Samir: thanks.
[15:52] [15:52] Wrap-up and recap of next steps.
